df["Change %"] = df["Change %"].astype(str).str.replace("%", "").astype(float)
df['Price'] = df['Price'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['High'] = df['High'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['Low'] = df['Low'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['Open'] = df['Open'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
 
# Cálculo de retorno (Return)
df["Return"] = df["Price"].pct_change()
 
# Reemplazar el primer NaN de Return por 0
df["Return"].iloc[0] = 0
 
# Cálculo de retorno acumulado
df["Cumulative_Return"] = df["Return"].cumsum()
 
# Cálculo de volatilidad en ventanas móviles
windows = [7, 14, 21, 28]
for w in windows:
    df[f"Volatility_{w}d"] = df["Return"].rolling(window=w, min_periods=1).std()
 
df.fillna(method='bfill', inplace=True)
df.fillna(method='ffill', inplace=True)
df.rename(columns={'Vol.': 'Volume', 'Change %': 'Change'}, inplace=True)
df = df[["Cumulative_Return"]]

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2) División del dataset en Train (70%), Validación (15%) y Test (15%)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
train_ratio = 0.70
val_ratio = 0.15
test_ratio = 0.15  # = 1 - train_ratio - val_ratio

total_data = len(df)
train_size = int(total_data * train_ratio)
val_size = int(total_data * val_ratio)

train = df.iloc[:train_size]
validation = df.iloc[train_size : train_size + val_size]
test = df.iloc[train_size + val_size :]

print(f"Tamaño de train: {len(train)}")
print(f"Tamaño de validación: {len(validation)}")
print(f"Tamaño de test: {len(test)}")

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3) Ajustar el modelo ARIMA (3, 1, 1) con la serie Cumulative_Return
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
model_cumulative = ARIMA(train["Cumulative_Return"], order=(3, 1, 1))  # Usamos p=3, d=1, q=1
fitted_model_cumulative = model_cumulative.fit()

# Generar predicciones para validación
val_predictions = fitted_model_cumulative.forecast(steps=len(validation))

# Calcular métricas de error
mae_cumulative = mean_absolute_error(validation["Cumulative_Return"], val_predictions)
mse_cumulative = mean_squared_error(validation["Cumulative_Return"], val_predictions)
rmse_cumulative = np.sqrt(mse_cumulative)
mape_cumulative = (np.abs(validation["Cumulative_Return"].values.flatten() - val_predictions.values.flatten()) / validation["Cumulative_Return"].values.flatten()).mean() * 100
r2_cumulative = r2_score(validation["Cumulative_Return"], val_predictions)

# Mostrar las métricas
metrics_df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Métrica": ["MAPE", "MAE", "RMSE", "MSE", "R^2"],
    "Valor": [mape_cumulative, mae_cumulative, rmse_cumulative, mse_cumulative, r2_cumulative]
})

print("\nMétricas del modelo ARIMA(3, 1, 1):")
print(metrics_df)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4) Gráficos de la predicción vs datos reales
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 6))
plt.plot(train.index, train["Cumulative_Return"], label="Entrenamiento")
plt.plot(validation.index, validation["Cumulative_Return"], label="Validación")
plt.plot(test.index, test["Cumulative_Return"], label="Test")

# Predicciones
plt.plot(validation.index, val_predictions, '--', label="Predicción Validación ARIMA(3, 1, 1)")

plt.legend()
plt.title("Predicción vs Datos Reales (ARIMA(3,1,1) para Cumulative_Return)")
plt.xlabel("Fecha")
plt.ylabel("Retorno Acumulado")
plt.show()

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5) ACF de los residuos del conjunto de TEST
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
residuals_test = test["Cumulative_Return"] - val_predictions
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
acf_vals_test = acf(residuals_test, nlags=30)
plt.stem(range(31), acf_vals_test, basefmt=" ")
plt.axhline(y=0, linestyle="--", color="gray")
plt.title("ACF de Residuos (Test) - ARIMA(3,1,1)")
plt.show()

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6) Pruebas de hipótesis sobre los residuos de ENTRENAMIENTO
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Residuos de entrenamiento
residuals_train = train["Cumulative_Return"] - fitted_model_cumulative.fittedvalues

# Prueba de independencia: Ljung-Box (con 10 lags)
ljung_box_p = acorr_ljungbox(residuals_train, lags=[10], return_df=True).iloc[0, 1]

# Prueba de normalidad: Jarque-Bera
jb_p = jarque_bera(residuals_train)[1]

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7) Tabla resumen de métricas (Train) y pruebas de hipótesis
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
metrics_df = pd.DataFrame({
    "MAPE": [mape_cumulative],
    "MAE": [mae_cumulative],
    "RMSE": [rmse_cumulative],
    "MSE": [mse_cumulative],
    "R2": [r2_cumulative],
    "Ljung-Box p-value": [ljung_box_p],
    "Jarque-Bera p-value": [jb_p]
})

print("\nMétricas del modelo (Entrenamiento) + Pruebas de hipótesis:")
print(metrics_df)

GARCH (Usando Rolling)

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from arch import arch_model
from statsmodels.graphics.tsaplots import plot_acf
from statsmodels.graphics.gofplots import qqplot
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.stats.diagnostic import acorr_ljungbox
from scipy import stats
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error, mean_squared_error, r2_score

# Reading data
data_url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lihkir/Data/refs/heads/main/Bitcoin%20Historical%20Data.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(data_url, parse_dates=['Date'], index_col='Date')

# Sort by date in order upward
df.sort_index(inplace=True)

# Function to convert volume to number
def parse_volume_str(vol_str):
    if not isinstance(vol_str, str):
        return vol_str
    vol_str = vol_str.replace(",", "").strip()
    if vol_str.endswith('K'):
        return float(vol_str[:-1]) * 1e3
    elif vol_str.endswith('M'):
        return float(vol_str[:-1]) * 1e6
    elif vol_str.endswith('B'):
        return float(vol_str[:-1]) * 1e9
    else:
        return float(vol_str)

# Apply cleanup function
df["Vol."] = df["Vol."].apply(parse_volume_str)
df["Change %"] = df["Change %"].astype(str).str.replace("%", "").astype(float)
df['Price'] = df['Price'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['High'] = df['High'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['Low'] = df['Low'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['Open'] = df['Open'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Return calculation (Return)
df["Return"] = df["Price"].pct_change().fillna(0)

# Cumulative Return Calculation
df["Cumulative_Return"] = df["Return"].cumsum()

# Volatility Calculation in Rolling Windows
windows = [7, 14, 21, 28]
for w in windows:
    df[f"Volatility_{w}d"] = df["Return"].rolling(window=w, min_periods=1).std()

# Print data info to verify
print(f"Dataset shape: {df.shape}")
print(f"Date range: {df.index.min()} to {df.index.max()}")
print(f"Columns: {df.columns.tolist()}")
print(df.head())

# Fix for NaN and zero values in series
def clean_series_for_garch(series):
    # Replace zeros and NaNs with small value to avoid GARCH issues
    series = series.replace(0, 1e-5)
    series = series.fillna(1e-5)
    return series

# Safer metrics calculation function
def calculate_metrics(y_true, y_pred):
    # Handle potential issues with division by zero
    try:
        # Replace zeros in y_true to avoid division by zero in MAPE
        y_true_safe = np.where(y_true == 0, 1e-10, y_true)
        mape = np.mean(np.abs((y_true_safe - y_pred) / y_true_safe)) * 100
    except:
        mape = np.nan
    
    mae = mean_absolute_error(y_true, y_pred)
    rmse = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_true, y_pred))
    mse = mean_squared_error(y_true, y_pred)
    
    try:
        r2 = r2_score(y_true, y_pred)
    except:
        r2 = np.nan
        
    return {'MAPE': mape, 'MAE': mae, 'RMSE': rmse, 'MSE': mse, 'R2': r2}

# Function to run statistical tests safely
def run_tests(residuals):
    # Make sure residuals don't contain NaN
    residuals = pd.Series(residuals).fillna(0).values
    
    # Ljung-Box test
    try:
        ljung_box = acorr_ljungbox(residuals, lags=10)
        lb_pvalue = ljung_box['lb_pvalue'][9]  # p-value for lag 10
    except:
        lb_pvalue = np.nan
    
    # BDS test - directly calculate p-value from statsmodels
    try:
        from statsmodels.nonparametric.tests import bds
        bds_test = bds.bds(residuals, max_dim=5)
        bds_pvalue = bds_test[1][0]  # p-value
    except:
        try:
            # Alternative implementation if the above fails
            from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import bds
            bds_test = bds(residuals)
            bds_pvalue = bds_test[1][0]
        except:
            bds_pvalue = np.nan
    
    # Jarque-Bera test
    try:
        jb_test = stats.jarque_bera(residuals)
        jb_pvalue = jb_test[1]
    except:
        jb_pvalue = np.nan
    
    return {'Ljung-Box': lb_pvalue, 'BDS': bds_pvalue, 'Jarque-Bera': jb_pvalue}

# Function to plot residual diagnostics
def plot_residuals(residuals, title):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(18, 5))
    
    # Residual series
    axes[0].plot(residuals)
    axes[0].set_title(f'Residual Series - {title}')
    
    # QQ Plot
    qqplot(residuals, line='s', ax=axes[1])
    axes[1].set_title(f'QQ Plot - {title}')
    
    # ACF
    try:
        plot_acf(residuals, ax=axes[2])
        axes[2].set_title(f'ACF of Residuals - {title}')
    except:
        axes[2].text(0.5, 0.5, "ACF plot failed", ha='center')
        axes[2].set_title(f'ACF (Error) - {title}')
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.close()  # Close to prevent display in notebook environments
    return fig

# Function to run GARCH model and evaluate with improved error handling
def run_garch_analysis(series_name, series_data, val_sizes=[7, 14, 21, 28], test_sizes=[7, 14, 21, 28]):
    print(f"Starting analysis for {series_name}")
    results = {}
    
    # Clean the series for GARCH analysis
    series = clean_series_for_garch(series_data)
    
    # Loop through different validation and test sizes
    for val_size in val_sizes:
        for test_size in test_sizes:
            config_name = f"Val:{val_size}, Test:{test_size}"
            print(f"  Processing configuration: {config_name}")
            
            try:
                # Split the data
                N = len(series)
                train_end = N - (val_size + test_size)
                val_end = N - test_size
                
                if train_end <= 0 or val_end <= train_end:
                    print(f"    Invalid split for {config_name}, skipping...")
                    continue
                
                train_data = series[:train_end]
                val_data = series[train_end:val_end]
                test_data = series[val_end:]
                
                print(f"    Train size: {len(train_data)}, Val size: {len(val_data)}, Test size: {len(test_data)}")
                
                # Apply GARCH model - use a simpler model with GARCH(1,1) and constant mean
                try:
                    model = arch_model(train_data, vol='GARCH', p=1, q=1, mean='Constant', rescale=False)
                    model_fit = model.fit(disp='off', show_warning=False)
                    
                    # Extract residuals
                    residuals = model_fit.resid
                    
                    # Get conditional volatility forecast for validation set
                    forecast_val = model_fit.forecast(horizon=len(val_data))
                    val_predictions = forecast_val.mean.iloc[-len(val_data):].values
                    
                    # Update model with validation data for test predictions
                    train_val_data = pd.concat([train_data, val_data])
                    model_with_val = arch_model(train_val_data, vol='GARCH', p=1, q=1, mean='Constant', rescale=False)
                    model_fit_with_val = model_with_val.fit(disp='off', show_warning=False)
                    
                    # Get forecast for test set
                    forecast_test = model_fit_with_val.forecast(horizon=len(test_data))
                    test_predictions = forecast_test.mean.iloc[-len(test_data):].values
                    
                    # Calculate metrics
                    train_metrics = calculate_metrics(train_data.values[1:], train_data.values[1:] - residuals[1:])
                    val_metrics = calculate_metrics(val_data.values, val_predictions.flatten())
                    test_metrics = calculate_metrics(test_data.values, test_predictions.flatten())
                    
                    # Run tests on residuals
                    train_tests = run_tests(residuals)
                    
                    # Create plots
                    try:
                        fig = plot_residuals(residuals, f"{series_name} - {config_name}")
                    except Exception as plot_error:
                        print(f"    Error creating plots: {plot_error}")
                        fig = None
                    
                    # Store results
                    results[config_name] = {
                        'train_metrics': train_metrics,
                        'train_tests': train_tests,
                        'val_metrics': val_metrics,
                        'test_metrics': test_metrics,
                        'residuals_plot': fig
                    }
                    
                    print(f"    Successfully processed {config_name}")
                    
                except Exception as model_error:
                    print(f"    Error in GARCH model fitting: {model_error}")
                    results[config_name] = {'error': f"Model error: {str(model_error)}"}
                
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"    Error with {config_name}: {e}")
                results[config_name] = {'error': str(e)}
    
    return results

# Create summary tables function with error handling
def create_summary_tables(results):
    summary_tables = {}
    
    for series_name, series_results in results.items():
        train_metrics = []
        train_tests = []
        val_metrics = []
        test_metrics = []
        
        for config, result in series_results.items():
            if 'error' in result:
                print(f"Skipping {series_name} - {config} due to error: {result['error']}")
                continue
            
            # Training metrics and tests
            metrics_row = result['train_metrics'].copy()  # Make a copy to avoid modifying original
            metrics_row['Configuration'] = config
            train_metrics.append(metrics_row)
            
            tests_row = result['train_tests'].copy()  # Make a copy to avoid modifying original
            tests_row['Configuration'] = config
            train_tests.append(tests_row)
            
            # Validation metrics
            val_row = result['val_metrics'].copy()  # Make a copy to avoid modifying original
            val_row['Configuration'] = config
            val_metrics.append(val_row)
            
            # Test metrics
            test_row = result['test_metrics'].copy()  # Make a copy to avoid modifying original
            test_row['Configuration'] = config
            test_metrics.append(test_row)
        
        # Skip if no valid results
        if not train_metrics:
            print(f"No valid results for {series_name}, skipping summary tables")
            continue
        
        # Create DataFrames
        train_metrics_df = pd.DataFrame(train_metrics).set_index('Configuration')
        train_tests_df = pd.DataFrame(train_tests).set_index('Configuration')
        val_metrics_df = pd.DataFrame(val_metrics).set_index('Configuration')
        test_metrics_df = pd.DataFrame(test_metrics).set_index('Configuration')
        
        # Combine training metrics and tests
        train_summary = pd.concat([train_metrics_df, train_tests_df], axis=1)
        
        summary_tables[series_name] = {
            'train_summary': train_summary,
            'val_metrics': val_metrics_df,
            'test_metrics': test_metrics_df
        }
    
    return summary_tables

# Run analysis on a subset first to test
series_to_analyze = {
    'Price': df['Price'],
    'Cumulative_Return': df['Cumulative_Return'],
    'Volatility_7d': df['Volatility_7d'],
    'Volatility_14d': df['Volatility_14d'],
    'Volatility_21d': df['Volatility_21d'],
    'Volatility_28d': df['Volatility_28d']
}

# Use smaller sets of validation and test sizes for faster testing
val_sizes = [7, 14, 21, 28]
test_sizes = [7, 14, 21, 28]

# Run the analysis
all_results = {}
for name, series in series_to_analyze.items():
    print(f"\nRunning GARCH analysis for {name}...")
    all_results[name] = run_garch_analysis(name, series, val_sizes, test_sizes)

# Create summary tables
print("\nCreating summary tables...")
summary_tables = create_summary_tables(all_results)

# Display summary tables
for series_name, tables in summary_tables.items():
    print(f"\n\n=== Summary for {series_name} ===")
    
    print("\nTraining Set Summary (Residuals):")
    print(tables['train_summary'].round(4))
    
    print("\nValidation Set Metrics:")
    print(tables['val_metrics'].round(4))
    
    print("\nTest Set Metrics:")
    print(tables['test_metrics'].round(4))

# Save results to CSV files
output_dir = "garch_results"
import os
if not os.path.exists(output_dir):
    os.makedirs(output_dir)

for series_name, tables in summary_tables.items():
    # Clean series name for filenames
    clean_name = series_name.replace("/", "_").replace(" ", "_")
    
    tables['train_summary'].to_csv(f"{output_dir}/{clean_name}_train_summary.csv")
    tables['val_metrics'].to_csv(f"{output_dir}/{clean_name}_val_metrics.csv")
    tables['test_metrics'].to_csv(f"{output_dir}/{clean_name}_test_metrics.csv")
    
    print(f"Saved results for {series_name} to CSV files")

print("\nAnalysis complete. Results saved to the 'garch'")

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from arch import arch_model
from statsmodels.graphics.tsaplots import plot_acf
from statsmodels.graphics.gofplots import qqplot
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.stats.diagnostic import acorr_ljungbox
from scipy import stats
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error, mean_squared_error, r2_score
import os

# Reading data
data_url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lihkir/Data/refs/heads/main/Bitcoin%20Historical%20Data.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(data_url, parse_dates=['Date'], index_col='Date')

# Sort by date in order upward
df.sort_index(inplace=True)

# Function to convert volume to number
def parse_volume_str(vol_str):
    if not isinstance(vol_str, str):
        return vol_str
    vol_str = vol_str.replace(",", "").strip()
    if vol_str.endswith('K'):
        return float(vol_str[:-1]) * 1e3
    elif vol_str.endswith('M'):
        return float(vol_str[:-1]) * 1e6
    elif vol_str.endswith('B'):
        return float(vol_str[:-1]) * 1e9
    else:
        return float(vol_str)

# Apply cleanup function
df["Vol."] = df["Vol."].apply(parse_volume_str)
df["Change %"] = df["Change %"].astype(str).str.replace("%", "").astype(float)
df['Price'] = df['Price'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['High'] = df['High'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['Low'] = df['Low'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['Open'] = df['Open'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Return calculation (Return)
df["Return"] = df["Price"].pct_change().fillna(0)

# Cumulative Return Calculation
df["Cumulative_Return"] = df["Return"].cumsum()

# Volatility Calculation in Rolling Windows
windows = [7, 14, 21, 28]
for w in windows:
    df[f"Volatility_{w}d"] = df["Return"].rolling(window=w, min_periods=1).std()

# Print data info to verify
print(f"Dataset shape: {df.shape}")
print(f"Date range: {df.index.min()} to {df.index.max()}")
print(f"Columns: {df.columns.tolist()}")
print(df.head())

# Fix for NaN and zero values in series
def clean_series_for_garch(series):
    # Replace zeros and NaNs with small value to avoid GARCH issues
    series = series.replace(0, 1e-5)
    series = series.fillna(1e-5)
    return series

# Safer metrics calculation function
def calculate_metrics(y_true, y_pred):
    # Handle potential issues with division by zero
    try:
        # Replace zeros in y_true to avoid division by zero in MAPE
        y_true_safe = np.where(y_true == 0, 1e-10, y_true)
        mape = np.mean(np.abs((y_true_safe - y_pred) / y_true_safe)) * 100
    except:
        mape = np.nan
    
    mae = mean_absolute_error(y_true, y_pred)
    rmse = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_true, y_pred))
    mse = mean_squared_error(y_true, y_pred)
    
    try:
        r2 = r2_score(y_true, y_pred)
    except:
        r2 = np.nan
        
    return {'MAPE': mape, 'MAE': mae, 'RMSE': rmse, 'MSE': mse, 'R2': r2}

# Function to run statistical tests safely
def run_tests(residuals):
    # Make sure residuals don't contain NaN
    residuals = pd.Series(residuals).fillna(0).values
    
    # Ljung-Box test
    try:
        ljung_box = acorr_ljungbox(residuals, lags=10)
        lb_pvalue = ljung_box['lb_pvalue'][9]  # p-value for lag 10
    except:
        lb_pvalue = np.nan
    
    # BDS test - directly calculate p-value from statsmodels
    try:
        from statsmodels.nonparametric.tests import bds
        bds_test = bds.bds(residuals, max_dim=5)
        bds_pvalue = bds_test[1][0]  # p-value
    except:
        try:
            # Alternative implementation if the above fails
            from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import bds
            bds_test = bds(residuals)
            bds_pvalue = bds_test[1][0]
        except:
            bds_pvalue = np.nan
    
    # Jarque-Bera test
    try:
        jb_test = stats.jarque_bera(residuals)
        jb_pvalue = jb_test[1]
    except:
        jb_pvalue = np.nan
    
    return {'Ljung-Box': lb_pvalue, 'BDS': bds_pvalue, 'Jarque-Bera': jb_pvalue}

# Function to plot residual diagnostics
def plot_residuals(residuals, title):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(18, 5))
    
    # Residual series
    axes[0].plot(residuals)
    axes[0].set_title(f'Residual Series - {title}')
    
    # QQ Plot
    qqplot(residuals, line='s', ax=axes[1])
    axes[1].set_title(f'QQ Plot - {title}')
    
    # ACF
    try:
        plot_acf(residuals, ax=axes[2])
        axes[2].set_title(f'ACF of Residuals - {title}')
    except:
        axes[2].text(0.5, 0.5, "ACF plot failed", ha='center')
        axes[2].set_title(f'ACF (Error) - {title}')
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    return fig

# Function to run GARCH model and evaluate with improved error handling
def run_garch_analysis(series_name, series_data, val_sizes=[7, 14, 21, 28], test_sizes=[7, 14, 21, 28]):
    print(f"Starting analysis for {series_name}")
    results = {}
    
    # Clean the series for GARCH analysis
    series = clean_series_for_garch(series_data)
    
    # Create directory for plots
    plots_dir = f"garch_results/plots/{series_name}"
    os.makedirs(plots_dir, exist_ok=True)
    
    # Loop through different validation and test sizes
    for val_size in val_sizes:
        for test_size in test_sizes:
            config_name = f"Val:{val_size}, Test:{test_size}"
            print(f"  Processing configuration: {config_name}")
            
            try:
                # Split the data
                N = len(series)
                train_end = N - (val_size + test_size)
                val_end = N - test_size
                
                if train_end <= 0 or val_end <= train_end:
                    print(f"    Invalid split for {config_name}, skipping...")
                    continue
                
                train_data = series[:train_end]
                val_data = series[train_end:val_end]
                test_data = series[val_end:]
                
                print(f"    Train size: {len(train_data)}, Val size: {len(val_data)}, Test size: {len(test_data)}")
                
                # Apply GARCH model - use a simpler model with GARCH(1,1) and constant mean
                try:
                    model = arch_model(train_data, vol='GARCH', p=1, q=1, mean='Constant', rescale=False)
                    model_fit = model.fit(disp='off', show_warning=False)
                    
                    # Print GARCH model summary
                    print("\nGARCH Model Summary:")
                    print(model_fit.summary().tables[1])
                    
                    # Extract residuals
                    residuals = model_fit.resid
                    
                    # Get conditional volatility forecast for validation set
                    forecast_val = model_fit.forecast(horizon=len(val_data))
                    val_predictions = forecast_val.mean.iloc[-len(val_data):].values
                    
                    # Update model with validation data for test predictions
                    train_val_data = pd.concat([train_data, val_data])
                    model_with_val = arch_model(train_val_data, vol='GARCH', p=1, q=1, mean='Constant', rescale=False)
                    model_fit_with_val = model_with_val.fit(disp='off', show_warning=False)
                    
                    # Get forecast for test set
                    forecast_test = model_fit_with_val.forecast(horizon=len(test_data))
                    test_predictions = forecast_test.mean.iloc[-len(test_data):].values
                    
                    # Calculate metrics
                    train_metrics = calculate_metrics(train_data.values[1:], train_data.values[1:] - residuals[1:])
                    val_metrics = calculate_metrics(val_data.values, val_predictions.flatten())
                    test_metrics = calculate_metrics(test_data.values, test_predictions.flatten())
                    
                    # Run tests on residuals
                    train_tests = run_tests(residuals)
                    
                    # Print metrics and tests
                    print("\nTraining Metrics:")
                    for metric, value in train_metrics.items():
                        print(f"  {metric}: {value:.4f}")
                    
                    print("\nTraining Tests:")
                    for test, value in train_tests.items():
                        print(f"  {test}: {value:.4f}")
                    
                    print("\nValidation Metrics:")
                    for metric, value in val_metrics.items():
                        print(f"  {metric}: {value:.4f}")
                    
                    print("\nTest Metrics:")
                    for metric, value in test_metrics.items():
                        print(f"  {metric}: {value:.4f}")
                    
                    # Create plots
                    fig = plot_residuals(residuals, f"{series_name} - {config_name}")
                    
                    # Display plot
                    plt.figure(figsize=(18, 5))
                    plt.show()
                    
                    # Save plot
                    plot_filename = f"{plots_dir}/{config_name.replace(':', '_')}.png"
                    fig.savefig(plot_filename)
                    print(f"    Plot saved to {plot_filename}")
                    
                    # Store results
                    results[config_name] = {
                        'train_metrics': train_metrics,
                        'train_tests': train_tests,
                        'val_metrics': val_metrics,
                        'test_metrics': test_metrics,
                        'residuals_plot': fig,
                        'model_summary': model_fit.summary().tables[1].as_text()
                    }
                    
                    print(f"    Successfully processed {config_name}")
                    
                except Exception as model_error:
                    print(f"    Error in GARCH model fitting: {model_error}")
                    results[config_name] = {'error': f"Model error: {str(model_error)}"}
                
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"    Error with {config_name}: {e}")
                results[config_name] = {'error': str(e)}
    
    return results

# Create summary tables function with error handling
def create_summary_tables(results):
    summary_tables = {}
    
    for series_name, series_results in results.items():
        train_metrics = []
        train_tests = []
        val_metrics = []
        test_metrics = []
        
        for config, result in series_results.items():
            if 'error' in result:
                print(f"Skipping {series_name} - {config} due to error: {result['error']}")
                continue
            
            # Training metrics and tests
            metrics_row = result['train_metrics'].copy()  # Make a copy to avoid modifying original
            metrics_row['Configuration'] = config
            train_metrics.append(metrics_row)
            
            tests_row = result['train_tests'].copy()  # Make a copy to avoid modifying original
            tests_row['Configuration'] = config
            train_tests.append(tests_row)
            
            # Validation metrics
            val_row = result['val_metrics'].copy()  # Make a copy to avoid modifying original
            val_row['Configuration'] = config
            val_metrics.append(val_row)
            
            # Test metrics
            test_row = result['test_metrics'].copy()  # Make a copy to avoid modifying original
            test_row['Configuration'] = config
            test_metrics.append(test_row)
        
        # Skip if no valid results
        if not train_metrics:
            print(f"No valid results for {series_name}, skipping summary tables")
            continue
        
        # Create DataFrames
        train_metrics_df = pd.DataFrame(train_metrics).set_index('Configuration')
        train_tests_df = pd.DataFrame(train_tests).set_index('Configuration')
        val_metrics_df = pd.DataFrame(val_metrics).set_index('Configuration')
        test_metrics_df = pd.DataFrame(test_metrics).set_index('Configuration')
        
        # Combine training metrics and tests
        train_summary = pd.concat([train_metrics_df, train_tests_df], axis=1)
        
        summary_tables[series_name] = {
            'train_summary': train_summary,
            'val_metrics': val_metrics_df,
            'test_metrics': test_metrics_df
        }
    
    return summary_tables

# Create output directory
output_dir = "garch_results"
if not os.path.exists(output_dir):
    os.makedirs(output_dir)
    # Let's run on just one series for quick testing
# Uncomment to run all series
series_to_analyze = {
    'Price': df['Price'],
    'Cumulative_Return': df['Cumulative_Return'],
    'Volatility_7d': df['Volatility_7d']
    # 'Volatility_14d': df['Volatility_14d'],
    # 'Volatility_21d': df['Volatility_21d'],
    # 'Volatility_28d': df['Volatility_28d']
}

# Use smaller sets of validation and test sizes for faster testing
# Just one combination for quick testing
val_sizes = [7]  # [7, 14, 21, 28]
test_sizes = [7]  # [7, 14, 21, 28]

# Run the analysis
all_results = {}
for name, series in series_to_analyze.items():
    print(f"\nRunning GARCH analysis for {name}...")
    all_results[name] = run_garch_analysis(name, series, val_sizes, test_sizes)

# Create summary tables
print("\nCreating summary tables...")
summary_tables = create_summary_tables(all_results)

# Display summary tables
for series_name, tables in summary_tables.items():
    print(f"\n\n=== Summary for {series_name} ===")
    
    print("\nTraining Set Summary (Residuals):")
    print(tables['train_summary'].round(4))
    
    print("\nValidation Set Metrics:")
    print(tables['val_metrics'].round(4))
    
    print("\nTest Set Metrics:")
    print(tables['test_metrics'].round(4))

# Generate visual summary for each series
for series_name, tables in summary_tables.items():
    print(f"\nGenerating visualizations for {series_name}...")
    
    # Heatmap of training metrics
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
    sns.heatmap(tables['train_summary'].iloc[:, :5], annot=True, cmap='viridis', fmt='.4f')
    plt.title(f'Training Metrics Heatmap - {series_name}')
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(f"{output_dir}/{series_name}_train_metrics_heatmap.png")
    plt.show()
    
    # Heatmap of test metrics
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
    sns.heatmap(tables['test_metrics'], annot=True, cmap='viridis', fmt='.4f')
    plt.title(f'Test Metrics Heatmap - {series_name}')
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(f"{output_dir}/{series_name}_test_metrics_heatmap.png")
    plt.show()

# Save results to CSV files
for series_name, tables in summary_tables.items():
    # Clean series name for filenames
    clean_name = series_name.replace("/", "_").replace(" ", "_")
    
    tables['train_summary'].to_csv(f"{output_dir}/{clean_name}_train_summary.csv")
    tables['val_metrics'].to_csv(f"{output_dir}/{clean_name}_val_metrics.csv")
    tables['test_metrics'].to_csv(f"{output_dir}/{clean_name}_test_metrics.csv")
    
    print(f"Saved results for {series_name} to CSV files")

# Save model summaries and additional information to text files
for series_name, series_results in all_results.items():
    clean_name = series_name.replace("/", "_").replace(" ", "_")
    
    with open(f"{output_dir}/{clean_name}_model_summaries.txt", "w") as f:
        f.write(f"GARCH Model Summaries for {series_name}\n")
        f.write("="*80 + "\n\n")
        
        for config, result in series_results.items():
            if 'error' in result:
                f.write(f"Configuration: {config}\n")
                f.write(f"Error: {result['error']}\n\n")
            else:
                f.write(f"Configuration: {config}\n")
                f.write("Model Summary:\n")
                f.write(result.get('model_summary', 'Summary not available'))
                f.write("\n\n")
                
    print(f"Saved model summaries for {series_name}")

# Full analysis complete
print("\nFull GARCH analysis complete. Results saved to the 'garch_results' directory.")
print("To run the full analysis on all series and configurations, uncomment the series and uncomment the full val_sizes and test_sizes lists.")

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from arch import arch_model
from statsmodels.graphics.tsaplots import plot_acf, plot_pacf
from statsmodels.graphics.gofplots import qqplot
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.stats.diagnostic import acorr_ljungbox
from scipy import stats
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error, mean_squared_error, r2_score

# Reading data
data_url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lihkir/Data/refs/heads/main/Bitcoin%20Historical%20Data.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(data_url, parse_dates=['Date'], index_col='Date')

# Sort by date in order upward
df.sort_index(inplace=True)

# Function to convert volume to number
def parse_volume_str(vol_str):
    if not isinstance(vol_str, str):
        return vol_str
    vol_str = vol_str.replace(",", "").strip()
    if vol_str.endswith('K'):
        return float(vol_str[:-1]) * 1e3
    elif vol_str.endswith('M'):
        return float(vol_str[:-1]) * 1e6
    elif vol_str.endswith('B'):
        return float(vol_str[:-1]) * 1e9
    else:
        return float(vol_str)

# Apply cleanup function
df["Vol."] = df["Vol."].apply(parse_volume_str)
df["Change %"] = df["Change %"].astype(str).str.replace("%", "").astype(float)
df['Price'] = df['Price'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['High'] = df['High'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['Low'] = df['Low'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['Open'] = df['Open'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Return calculation (Return)
df["Return"] = df["Price"].pct_change().fillna(0)

# Cumulative Return Calculation
df["Cumulative_Return"] = df["Return"].cumsum()

# Volatility Calculation in Rolling Windows
windows = [7, 14, 21, 28]
for w in windows:
    df[f"Volatility_{w}d"] = df["Return"].rolling(window=w, min_periods=1).std()

# Print data info to verify
print(f"Dataset shape: {df.shape}")
print(f"Date range: {df.index.min()} to {df.index.max()}")
print(f"Columns: {df.columns.tolist()}")
print(df.head())

# Fix for NaN and zero values in series
def clean_series_for_garch(series):
    # Replace zeros and NaNs with small values to avoid GARCH issues
    series = series.replace(0, 1e-5)
    series = series.fillna(1e-5)
    return series

# Safer metrics calculation function
def calculate_metrics(y_true, y_pred):
    # Handle potential issues with division by zero
    try:
        # Replace zeros in y_true to avoid division by zero in MAPE
        y_true_safe = np.where(y_true == 0, 1e-10, y_true)
        mape = np.mean(np.abs((y_true_safe - y_pred) / y_true_safe)) * 100
    except:
        mape = np.nan

    mae = mean_absolute_error(y_true, y_pred)
    rmse = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_true, y_pred))
    mse = mean_squared_error(y_true, y_pred)

    try:
        r2 = r2_score(y_true, y_pred)
    except:
        r2 = np.nan

    return {'MAPE': mape, 'MAE': mae, 'RMSE': rmse, 'MSE': mse, 'R2': r2}

# Function to run statistical tests safely
def run_tests(residuals):
    # Make sure residuals don't contain NaN
    residuals = pd.Series(residuals).fillna(0).values

    # Ljung-Box test
    try:
        ljung_box = acorr_ljungbox(residuals, lags=10)
        lb_pvalue = ljung_box['lb_pvalue'][9]  # p-value for lag 10
    except:
        lb_pvalue = np.nan

    # BDS test - directly calculate p-value from statsmodels
    try:
        from statsmodels.nonparametric.tests import bds
        bds_test = bds.bds(residuals, max_dim=5)
        bds_pvalue = bds_test[1][0]  # p-value
    except:
        try:
            # Alternative implementation if the above fails
            from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import bds
            bds_test = bds(residuals)
            bds_pvalue = bds_test[1][0]
        except:
            bds_pvalue = np.nan

    # Jarque-Bera test
    try:
        jb_test = stats.jarque_bera(residuals)
        jb_pvalue = jb_test[1]
    except:
        jb_pvalue = np.nan

    return {'Ljung-Box': lb_pvalue, 'BDS': bds_pvalue, 'Jarque-Bera': jb_pvalue}

# Function to plot residual diagnostics
def plot_residuals(residuals, title):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 12))
    
    # Residual series
    axes[0, 0].plot(residuals)
    axes[0, 0].set_title(f'Residual Series - {title}')
    
    # QQ Plot
    qqplot(residuals, line='s', ax=axes[0, 1])
    axes[0, 1].set_title(f'QQ Plot - {title}')
    
    # Histogram
    axes[1, 0].hist(residuals, bins=30, alpha=0.7, density=True)
    x = np.linspace(min(residuals), max(residuals), 100)
    axes[1, 0].plot(x, stats.norm.pdf(x, np.mean(residuals), np.std(residuals)))
    axes[1, 0].set_title(f'Histogram - {title}')
    
    # ACF
    plot_acf(residuals, ax=axes[1, 1], lags=20)
    axes[1, 1].set_title(f'ACF - {title}')
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

# Function to run GARCH model with specified parameters
def run_garch_model(returns, p, q, mean_model="Constant", vol_model="GARCH", 
                    dist="normal", train_size=0.8, test_windows=[30, 60, 90]):
    """
    Run GARCH model with specified parameters
    
    Parameters:
    - returns: Series of returns
    - p: ARCH term order
    - q: GARCH term order
    - mean_model: Mean model ("Constant", "Zero", "AR", etc.)
    - vol_model: Volatility model ("GARCH", "EGARCH", "GJR", etc.)
    - dist: Error distribution ("normal", "t", "skewt")
    - train_size: Proportion of data for training
    - test_windows: List of test window sizes to evaluate
    
    Returns:
    - Dict containing model results and forecasts
    """
    # Clean data
    clean_returns = clean_series_for_garch(returns)
    
    # Split data
    train_cutoff = int(len(clean_returns) * train_size)
    train_data = clean_returns[:train_cutoff]
    test_data = clean_returns[train_cutoff:]
    
    # Create model
    try:
        model = arch_model(train_data, vol="GARCH", p=p, q=q, mean=mean_model, 
                          dist=dist)
        # Using EGARCH or GJR for asymmetric models
        if vol_model.upper() == "EGARCH":
            model = arch_model(train_data, vol="EGARCH", p=p, q=q, mean=mean_model, 
                              dist=dist)
        elif vol_model.upper() == "GJR" or vol_model.upper() == "GJRGARCH":
            model = arch_model(train_data, vol="GARCH", p=p, o=1, q=q, mean=mean_model, 
                              dist=dist)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error creating model: {e}")
        return None
    
    # Fit model
    try:
        results = model.fit(disp='off')
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error fitting model: {e}")
        return None
    
    # Generate forecasts for different test windows
    forecasts = {}
    for window in test_windows:
        # Make sure window isn't larger than test data
        if window > len(test_data):
            continue
        
        try:
            # Forecasting
            forecast = results.forecast(horizon=window, reindex=False)
            # Extract variance (volatility squared)
            variance_forecast = forecast.variance.iloc[-1].values
            # Get volatility forecast
            volatility_forecast = np.sqrt(variance_forecast)
            
            # Evaluate forecast
            actual_volatility = test_data[:window].rolling(window=5).std().dropna()
            pred_volatility = pd.Series(volatility_forecast, 
                                     index=test_data.index[:window])
            
            # Calculate metrics
            if len(actual_volatility) > 0 and len(pred_volatility) > 0:
                # Align index
                common_idx = actual_volatility.index.intersection(pred_volatility.index)
                if len(common_idx) > 0:
                    act_vol = actual_volatility.loc[common_idx]
                    pred_vol = pred_volatility.loc[common_idx]
                    metrics = calculate_metrics(act_vol.values, pred_vol.values)
                    forecasts[window] = {
                        'forecast': pred_volatility,
                        'actual': actual_volatility,
                        'metrics': metrics
                    }
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error in forecasting for window {window}: {e}")
    
    # Model summary
    model_summary = {
        'aic': results.aic,
        'bic': results.bic,
        'params': results.params.to_dict(),
        'residuals': results.resid,
        'conditional_volatility': results.conditional_volatility,
        'test_statistics': run_tests(results.resid)
    }
    
    return {
        'model': results,
        'summary': model_summary,
        'forecasts': forecasts
    }

# Function to compare multiple GARCH models
def compare_garch_models(returns, models_to_test, train_sizes=[0.8], test_windows=[30, 60, 90]):
    """
    Compare multiple GARCH models
    
    Parameters:
    - returns: Series of returns
    - models_to_test: List of dictionaries containing model specifications
    - train_sizes: List of train/test split ratios
    - test_windows: List of forecast horizons
    
    Returns:
    - DataFrame with model comparison results
    """
    results = []
    
    for model_spec in models_to_test:
        model_name = f"{model_spec['vol_model']}({model_spec['p']},{model_spec['q']})-{model_spec['dist']}"
        print(f"Running {model_name}...")
        
        for train_size in train_sizes:
            try:
                model_result = run_garch_model(
                    returns=returns,
                    p=model_spec['p'],
                    q=model_spec['q'],
                    mean_model=model_spec.get('mean_model', 'Constant'),
                    vol_model=model_spec['vol_model'],
                    dist=model_spec['dist'],
                    train_size=train_size,
                    test_windows=test_windows
                )
                
                if model_result is None:
                    continue
                
                # Extract key metrics
                for window, forecast in model_result['forecasts'].items():
                    row = {
                        'Model': model_name,
                        'Train Size': train_size,
                        'Test Window': window,
                        'AIC': model_result['summary']['aic'],
                        'BIC': model_result['summary']['bic'],
                        'Ljung-Box p-value': model_result['summary']['test_statistics']['Ljung-Box'],
                        'Jarque-Bera p-value': model_result['summary']['test_statistics']['Jarque-Bera']
                    }
                    
                    # Add forecast metrics
                    for metric, value in forecast['metrics'].items():
                        row[metric] = value
                    
                    results.append(row)
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Error processing {model_name} with train size {train_size}: {e}")
    
    # Create DataFrame from results
    if results:
        return pd.DataFrame(results)
    else:
        return pd.DataFrame()

# Function to plot comparative results
def plot_comparative_results(comparison_df, metric='RMSE', figsize=(14, 8)):
    """
    Plot comparative results of different models
    
    Parameters:
    - comparison_df: DataFrame with model comparison results
    - metric: Metric to plot (default: RMSE)
    - figsize: Figure size tuple
    """
    if comparison_df.empty:
        print("No results to plot")
        return
    
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(comparison_df['Test Window'].unique()), figsize=figsize)
    
    for i, window in enumerate(sorted(comparison_df['Test Window'].unique())):
        window_data = comparison_df[comparison_df['Test Window'] == window]
        
        # Sort by metric
        window_data = window_data.sort_values(by=metric)
        
        # Plot
        ax = axes[i] if len(comparison_df['Test Window'].unique()) > 1 else axes
        sns.barplot(x='Model', y=metric, data=window_data, ax=ax)
        ax.set_title(f'Test Window: {window} days')
        ax.set_xticklabels(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=45, ha='right')
        ax.set_ylabel(metric)
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

# Function to visualize forecast vs actual
def plot_forecast_vs_actual(returns, model_results, window_size, figsize=(14, 8)):
    """
    Plot forecast vs actual volatility
    
    Parameters:
    - returns: Series of returns
    - model_results: Dict containing model results
    - window_size: Test window size to plot
    - figsize: Figure size tuple
    """
    if window_size not in model_results['forecasts']:
        print(f"No forecast available for window size {window_size}")
        return
    
    forecast = model_results['forecasts'][window_size]
    
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=figsize)
    
    # Plot actual volatility
    forecast['actual'].plot(ax=ax, label='Actual Volatility', color='blue', alpha=0.7)
    
    # Plot forecast volatility
    forecast['forecast'].plot(ax=ax, label='Forecast Volatility', color='red', linestyle='--')
    
    ax.set_title(f'Forecast vs Actual Volatility (Window: {window_size} days)')
    ax.set_xlabel('Date')
    ax.set_ylabel('Volatility')
    ax.legend()
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    
    # Print metrics
    print(f"Forecast Metrics for {window_size}-day window:")
    for metric, value in forecast['metrics'].items():
        print(f"{metric}: {value:.4f}")

# Function to run analysis on all series
def run_complete_analysis(df, series_to_analyze=None, train_sizes=[0.8], test_windows=[30, 60, 90]):
    """
    Run complete analysis on multiple time series
    
    Parameters:
    - df: DataFrame containing the data
    - series_to_analyze: List of column names to analyze (if None, use returns and volatilities)
    - train_sizes: List of train/test split proportions
    - test_windows: List of forecast horizons
    
    Returns:
    - Dict containing results for each series
    """
    if series_to_analyze is None:
        # Default to returns and volatilities
        series_to_analyze = ["Return"] + [f"Volatility_{w}d" for w in windows]
    
    results = {}
    
    # Define models to test
    garch_models = [
        # Standard GARCH models
        {'p': 1, 'q': 1, 'vol_model': 'GARCH', 'dist': 'normal'},
        {'p': 1, 'q': 1, 'vol_model': 'GARCH', 'dist': 't'},
        {'p': 2, 'q': 2, 'vol_model': 'GARCH', 'dist': 'normal'},
        {'p': 2, 'q': 2, 'vol_model': 'GARCH', 'dist': 't'},
        
        # Asymmetric GARCH models
        {'p': 1, 'q': 1, 'vol_model': 'EGARCH', 'dist': 'normal'},
        {'p': 1, 'q': 1, 'vol_model': 'EGARCH', 'dist': 't'},
        {'p': 2, 'q': 2, 'vol_model': 'EGARCH', 'dist': 'normal'},
        {'p': 2, 'q': 2, 'vol_model': 'EGARCH', 'dist': 't'},
        
        # GJR-GARCH models
        {'p': 1, 'q': 1, 'vol_model': 'GJR', 'dist': 'normal'},
        {'p': 1, 'q': 1, 'vol_model': 'GJR', 'dist': 't'},
        {'p': 2, 'q': 2, 'vol_model': 'GJR', 'dist': 'normal'},
        {'p': 2, 'q': 2, 'vol_model': 'GJR', 'dist': 't'},
    ]
    
    for series_name in series_to_analyze:
        print(f"\n{'='*50}")
        print(f"Analyzing series: {series_name}")
        print(f"{'='*50}")
        
        # Get series
        series = df[series_name]
        
        # Run comparison
        comparison_results = compare_garch_models(
            returns=series,
            models_to_test=garch_models,
            train_sizes=train_sizes,
            test_windows=test_windows
        )
        
        # Store results
        results[series_name] = comparison_results
        
        # Plot results for this series
        for metric in ['RMSE', 'MAE', 'MAPE']:
            try:
                print(f"\nComparing models by {metric}:")
                plot_comparative_results(comparison_results, metric=metric)
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Error plotting comparative results for {metric}: {e}")
    
    return results

# Function to plot model diagnostics
def plot_model_diagnostics(model_result, title="Model Diagnostics"):
    """
    Plot model diagnostics
    
    Parameters:
    - model_result: Dict containing model results
    - title: Plot title
    """
    # Get model and residuals
    model = model_result['model']
    residuals = model_result['summary']['residuals']
    cond_vol = model_result['summary']['conditional_volatility']
    
    # Create figure
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(18, 12))
    
    # Returns and conditional volatility
    axes[0, 0].plot(residuals**2, label='Squared Returns', alpha=0.5)
    axes[0, 0].plot(cond_vol**2, label='Conditional Variance', color='red')
    axes[0, 0].set_title('Returns vs Conditional Volatility')
    axes[0, 0].legend()
    
    # Standardized residuals
    std_resid = residuals / cond_vol
    axes[0, 1].plot(std_resid)
    axes[0, 1].set_title('Standardized Residuals')
    
    # QQ plot of standardized residuals
    qqplot(std_resid, line='s', ax=axes[1, 0])
    axes[1, 0].set_title('QQ Plot of Standardized Residuals')
    
    # Histogram of standardized residuals
    axes[1, 1].hist(std_resid, bins=30, alpha=0.7, density=True)
    x = np.linspace(min(std_resid), max(std_resid), 100)
    axes[1, 1].plot(x, stats.norm.pdf(x, np.mean(std_resid), np.std(std_resid)))
    axes[1, 1].set_title('Histogram of Standardized Residuals')
    
    # ACF of standardized residuals
    plot_acf(std_resid, ax=axes[2, 0], lags=20)
    axes[2, 0].set_title('ACF of Standardized Residuals')
    
    # ACF of squared standardized residuals
    plot_acf(std_resid**2, ax=axes[2, 1], lags=20)
    axes[2, 1].set_title('ACF of Squared Standardized Residuals')
    
    plt.suptitle(title, fontsize=16)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.subplots_adjust(top=0.93)
    plt.show()

# Function to find the best model for each series and window
def find_best_models(all_results, metric='RMSE'):
    """
    Find the best model for each series and window
    
    Parameters:
    - all_results: Dict containing results for each series
    - metric: Metric to use for ranking (default: RMSE)
    
    Returns:
    - DataFrame with best models
    """
    best_models = []
    
    for series_name, results in all_results.items():
        if results.empty:
            continue
            
        for window in results['Test Window'].unique():
            window_data = results[results['Test Window'] == window]
            
            # Get best model by metric
            best_idx = window_data[metric].idxmin()
            if pd.isna(best_idx):
                continue
                
            best_row = window_data.loc[best_idx].copy()
            best_row['Series'] = series_name
            best_models.append(best_row)
    
    if not best_models:
        return pd.DataFrame()
        
    return pd.DataFrame(best_models)

# Function to create comparative visualizations
def create_comparative_visualizations(all_results, metric='RMSE'):
    """
    Create comparative visualizations of model performance
    
    Parameters:
    - all_results: Dict containing results for each series
    - metric: Metric to use for comparison
    """
    # Get all series names
    series_names = list(all_results.keys())
    
    # Get all unique window sizes
    all_windows = set()
    for results in all_results.values():
        if not results.empty:
            all_windows.update(results['Test Window'].unique())
    all_windows = sorted(all_windows)
    
    # Get all unique models
    all_models = set()
    for results in all_results.values():
        if not results.empty:
            all_models.update(results['Model'].unique())
    
    # Create comparison plots for each window size
    for window in all_windows:
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 8))
        
        data_to_plot = []
        for series_name in series_names:
            results = all_results[series_name]
            if results.empty:
                continue
                
            window_data = results[results['Test Window'] == window]
            if window_data.empty:
                continue
                
            for _, row in window_data.iterrows():
                data_to_plot.append({
                    'Series': series_name,
                    'Model': row['Model'],
                    metric: row[metric]
                })
        
        if not data_to_plot:
            plt.close(fig)
            continue
            
        plot_df = pd.DataFrame(data_to_plot)
        
        # Create heatmap data
        heatmap_data = plot_df.pivot(index='Model', columns='Series', values=metric)
        
        # Plot heatmap
        sns.heatmap(heatmap_data, annot=True, cmap='YlGnBu', fmt='.3f', ax=ax)
        ax.set_title(f'Model Performance ({metric}) - Window Size: {window} days')
        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()

# Main analysis function - run step by step to avoid memory issues
def run_step_by_step_analysis(df):
    """
    Run the analysis step by step to avoid memory issues
    
    Parameters:
    - df: DataFrame containing the data
    """
    # Step 1: Basic data exploration and visualization
    print("Step 1: Basic data exploration and visualization")
    
    # Plot price and returns
    plt.figure(figsize=(14, 10))
    
    plt.subplot(2, 1, 1)
    df['Price'].plot()
    plt.title('Bitcoin Price')
    
    plt.subplot(2, 1, 2)
    df['Return'].plot()
    plt.title('Bitcoin Returns')
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    
    # Plot volatility
    plt.figure(figsize=(14, 6))
    for w in windows:
        df[f"Volatility_{w}d"].plot(label=f'{w}-day Volatility')
    plt.title('Rolling Volatility')
    plt.legend()
    plt.show()
    
    # Step 2: Run analysis on returns first
    print("\nStep 2: Running analysis on Bitcoin returns")
    returns_results = run_complete_analysis(
        df, 
        series_to_analyze=["Return"], 
        test_windows=[30, 60]
    )
    
    # Step 3: Find best models for returns
    print("\nStep 3: Finding best models for returns")
    best_returns_models = find_best_models(returns_results)
    print("Best models for returns:")
    print(best_returns_models)
    
    # Step 4: Run analysis on volatility series (one at a time)
    print("\nStep 4: Running analysis on volatility series")
    volatility_results = {}
    
    for w in windows:
        print(f"\nAnalyzing {w}-day volatility")
        series_name = f"Volatility_{w}d"
        vol_result = run_complete_analysis(
            df, 
            series_to_analyze=[series_name], 
            test_windows=[30]  # Use only 30-day window to save memory
        )
        volatility_results.update(vol_result)
    
    # Step 5: Find best models for volatility series
    print("\nStep 5: Finding best models for volatility series")
    best_vol_models = find_best_models(volatility_results)
    print("Best models for volatility:")
    print(best_vol_models)
    
    # Step 6: Create comparative visualizations
    print("\nStep 6: Creating comparative visualizations")
    
    # Combine results
    all_results = {**returns_results, **volatility_results}
    
    # Create visualizations
    create_comparative_visualizations(all_results)
    
    return {
        'returns_results': returns_results,
        'volatility_results': volatility_results,
        'best_returns_models': best_returns_models,
        'best_vol_models': best_vol_models
    }

# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":

    analysis_results = run_step_by_step_analysis(df)
    
    # Additional analysis can be performed on specific series and models

ARIMA (Usando Rolling)#

Precio

import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import acf, q_stat
from statsmodels.tsa.holtwinters import SimpleExpSmoothing
from statsmodels.graphics.tsaplots import plot_acf, plot_pacf
from statsmodels.stats.stattools import jarque_bera
from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error, mean_squared_error, r2_score
from scipy.stats import jarque_bera
from statsmodels.stats.diagnostic import acorr_ljungbox

import seaborn as sns
from statsmodels.tsa.arima.model import ARIMA

# 1. Lectura de datos y limpieza
data_url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lihkir/Data/refs/heads/main/Bitcoin%20Historical%20Data.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(data_url, parse_dates=['Date'], index_col='Date')

# Ordenar por fecha (índice) en orden ascendente
df.sort_index(inplace=True)

def parse_volume_str(vol_str):
    if not isinstance(vol_str, str):
        return vol_str
    vol_str = vol_str.replace(",", "").strip()
    if vol_str.endswith('K'):
        return float(vol_str[:-1]) * 1e3
    elif vol_str.endswith('M'):
        return float(vol_str[:-1]) * 1e6
    elif vol_str.endswith('B'):
        return float(vol_str[:-1]) * 1e9
    else:
        return float(vol_str)

df["Vol."] = df["Vol."].apply(parse_volume_str)
df["Change %"] = df["Change %"].astype(str).str.replace("%", "").astype(float)
df['Price'] = df['Price'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['High'] = df['High'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['Low'] = df['Low'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['Open'] = df['Open'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Cálculo de retorno (Return)
df["Return"] = df["Price"].pct_change()

# Reemplazar el primer NaN de Return por 0
df["Return"].iloc[0] = 0

# Cálculo de retorno acumulado
df["Cumulative_Return"] = df["Return"].cumsum()

# Cálculo de volatilidad en ventanas móviles
windows = [7, 14, 21, 28]
for w in windows:
    df[f"Volatility_{w}d"] = df["Return"].rolling(window=w, min_periods=1).std()

df.fillna(method='bfill', inplace=True)
df.fillna(method='ffill', inplace=True)
df.rename(columns={'Vol.': 'Volume', 'Change %': 'Change'}, inplace=True)

df = df[["Price"]]

# Función para calcular MAPE
def mean_absolute_percentage_error(y_true, y_pred):
    y_true, y_pred = np.array(y_true), np.array(y_pred)
    return np.mean(np.abs((y_true - y_pred) / y_true)) * 100

# Función para ARIMA con rolling forecasting
def arima_rolling(df, train_size, val_size, order):
    """
    Implementación de ARIMA con rolling forecasting sin ventanas fijas.

    Parámetros:
    - df: DataFrame con la serie temporal.
    - train_size: Tamaño del conjunto de entrenamiento en número de observaciones.
    - val_size: Tamaño del conjunto de validación en número de observaciones.
    - order: Orden del modelo ARIMA (p, d, q).

    Retorna:
    - Diccionario con métricas de error y predicciones.
    """
    # Dividir los datos en entrenamiento, validación y prueba
    train = df['Price'][:train_size].tolist()
    val = df['Price'][train_size:train_size + val_size].tolist()
    test = df['Price'][train_size + val_size:].tolist()

    val_dates = df.index[train_size:train_size + val_size]
    test_dates = df.index[train_size + val_size:]

    # Predicciones en validación y test con rolling forecasting
    val_predictions = []
    test_predictions = []

    # Fase de validación (rolling forecasting)
    for t in range(len(val)):
        model = ARIMA(train, order=order)
        model_fit = model.fit()
        forecast = model_fit.forecast()[0]  # Predicción de un solo punto
        val_predictions.append(forecast)
        train.append(val[t])  # Agregar el valor real para continuar el rolling

    # Evaluación en validación
    mae_val = mean_absolute_error(val, val_predictions)
    mse_val = mean_squared_error(val, val_predictions)
    rmse_val = np.sqrt(mse_val)
    mape_val = mean_absolute_percentage_error(val, val_predictions)
    r2_val = r2_score(val, val_predictions)

    # Fase de test (rolling forecasting)
    for t in range(len(test)):
        model = ARIMA(train, order=order)
        model_fit = model.fit()
        forecast = model_fit.forecast()[0]  # Predicción de un solo punto
        test_predictions.append(forecast)
        train.append(test[t])  # Agregar el valor real para continuar el rolling

    # Evaluación en test
    mae_test = mean_absolute_error(test, test_predictions)
    mse_test = mean_squared_error(test, test_predictions)
    rmse_test = np.sqrt(mse_test)
    mape_test = mean_absolute_percentage_error(test, test_predictions)
    r2_test = r2_score(test, test_predictions)

    # Visualización del modelo ARIMA
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
    sns.lineplot(x=df.index[:train_size], y=df['Price'][:train_size], label="Train", color='blue')
    sns.lineplot(x=val_dates, y=val, label="Validation", color='orange')
    sns.lineplot(x=test_dates, y=test, label="Test", color='green')
    sns.lineplot(x=val_dates, y=val_predictions, label="Forecast Validation", linestyle='dashed', color='red')
    sns.lineplot(x=test_dates, y=test_predictions, label="Forecast Test", linestyle='dashed', color='purple')
    plt.xlabel("Fecha")
    plt.ylabel("Price")
    plt.title("Predicción ARIMA con Rolling Forecasting")
    plt.legend()
    plt.show()

    return {
        "validación": {"MAPE": mape_val, "MAE": mae_val, "MSE": mse_val, "RMSE": rmse_val, "R²": r2_val},
        "test": {"MAPE": mape_test, "MAE": mae_test, "MSE": mse_test, "RMSE": rmse_test, "R²": r2_test},
        "residuals": model_fit.resid  # Se retornan los residuos para la segunda parte
    }

# Definir los tamaños de los conjuntos
train_size = int(len(df) * 0.6)  # 60% entrenamiento
val_size = int(len(df) * 0.2)  # 20% validación
test_size = len(df) - (train_size + val_size)  # 20% test

# Parámetros del modelo ARIMA
best_order = (0, 1, 0)  # Se puede ajustar según análisis previo

# Ejecutar el modelo con rolling forecasting
resultados = arima_rolling(df, train_size, val_size, best_order)

# Guardar los residuos para la segunda parte
residuals = resultados["residuals"]

# Pruebas estadísticas sobre residuos
ljung_box_pvalue = acorr_ljungbox(residuals, lags=[10], return_df=True)['lb_pvalue'].values[0]
jarque_bera_pvalue = jarque_bera(residuals)[1]

# Mostrar métricas
print("\nErrores en validación:")
for metric, value in resultados["validación"].items():
    print(f"{metric}: {value:.4f}")

print("\nErrores en test:")
for metric, value in resultados["test"].items():

import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import statsmodels.api as sm
from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import acf, q_stat
from statsmodels.tsa.holtwinters import SimpleExpSmoothing
from statsmodels.graphics.tsaplots import plot_acf, plot_pacf
from statsmodels.stats.stattools import jarque_bera
from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error, mean_squared_error, r2_score
from scipy.stats import jarque_bera
from statsmodels.stats.diagnostic import acorr_ljungbox

import seaborn as sns
from statsmodels.tsa.arima.model import ARIMA

# 1. Lectura de datos y limpieza
data_url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lihkir/Data/refs/heads/main/Bitcoin%20Historical%20Data.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(data_url, parse_dates=['Date'], index_col='Date')

# Ordenar por fecha (índice) en orden ascendente
df.sort_index(inplace=True)

def parse_volume_str(vol_str):
    if not isinstance(vol_str, str):
        return vol_str
    vol_str = vol_str.replace(",", "").strip()
    if vol_str.endswith('K'):
        return float(vol_str[:-1]) * 1e3
    elif vol_str.endswith('M'):
        return float(vol_str[:-1]) * 1e6
    elif vol_str.endswith('B'):
        return float(vol_str[:-1]) * 1e9
    else:
        return float(vol_str)

df["Vol."] = df["Vol."].apply(parse_volume_str)
df["Change %"] = df["Change %"].astype(str).str.replace("%", "").astype(float)
df['Price'] = df['Price'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['High'] = df['High'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['Low'] = df['Low'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)
df['Open'] = df['Open'].astype(str).str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Cálculo de retorno (Return)
df["Return"] = df["Price"].pct_change()

# Reemplazar el primer NaN de Return por 0
df["Return"].iloc[0] = 0

# Cálculo de retorno acumulado
df["Cumulative_Return"] = df["Return"].cumsum()

# Cálculo de volatilidad en ventanas móviles
windows = [7, 14, 21, 28]
for w in windows:
    df[f"Volatility_{w}d"] = df["Return"].rolling(window=w, min_periods=1).std()

df.fillna(method='bfill', inplace=True)
df.fillna(method='ffill', inplace=True)
df.rename(columns={'Vol.': 'Volume', 'Change %': 'Change'}, inplace=True)

df = df[["Cumulative_Return"]]

# Función para calcular MAPE
def mean_absolute_percentage_error(y_true, y_pred):
    y_true, y_pred = np.array(y_true), np.array(y_pred)
    return np.mean(np.abs((y_true - y_pred) / y_true)) * 100

# Función para ARIMA con rolling forecasting
def arima_rolling(df, train_size, val_size, order):
    """
    Implementación de ARIMA con rolling forecasting sin ventanas fijas.

    Parámetros:
    - df: DataFrame con la serie temporal.
    - train_size: Tamaño del conjunto de entrenamiento en número de observaciones.
    - val_size: Tamaño del conjunto de validación en número de observaciones.
    - order: Orden del modelo ARIMA (p, d, q).

    Retorna:
    - Diccionario con métricas de error y predicciones.
    """
    # Dividir los datos en entrenamiento, validación y prueba
    train = df['Cumulative_Return'][:train_size].tolist()
    val = df['Cumulative_Return'][train_size:train_size + val_size].tolist()
    test = df['Cumulative_Return'][train_size + val_size:].tolist()

    val_dates = df.index[train_size:train_size + val_size]
    test_dates = df.index[train_size + val_size:]

    # Predicciones en validación y test con rolling forecasting
    val_predictions = []
    test_predictions = []

    # Fase de validación (rolling forecasting)
    for t in range(len(val)):
        model = ARIMA(train, order=order)
        model_fit = model.fit()
        forecast = model_fit.forecast()[0]  # Predicción de un solo punto
        val_predictions.append(forecast)
        train.append(val[t])  # Agregar el valor real para continuar el rolling

    # Evaluación en validación
    mae_val = mean_absolute_error(val, val_predictions)
    mse_val = mean_squared_error(val, val_predictions)
    rmse_val = np.sqrt(mse_val)
    mape_val = mean_absolute_percentage_error(val, val_predictions)
    r2_val = r2_score(val, val_predictions)

    # Fase de test (rolling forecasting)
    for t in range(len(test)):
        model = ARIMA(train, order=order)
        model_fit = model.fit()
        forecast = model_fit.forecast()[0]  # Predicción de un solo punto
        test_predictions.append(forecast)
        train.append(test[t])  # Agregar el valor real para continuar el rolling

    # Evaluación en test
    mae_test = mean_absolute_error(test, test_predictions)
    mse_test = mean_squared_error(test, test_predictions)
    rmse_test = np.sqrt(mse_test)
    mape_test = mean_absolute_percentage_error(test, test_predictions)
    r2_test = r2_score(test, test_predictions)

    # Visualización del modelo ARIMA
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
    sns.lineplot(x=df.index[:train_size], y=df['Cumulative_Return'][:train_size], label="Train", color='blue')
    sns.lineplot(x=val_dates, y=val, label="Validation", color='orange')
    sns.lineplot(x=test_dates, y=test, label="Test", color='green')
    sns.lineplot(x=val_dates, y=val_predictions, label="Forecast Validation", linestyle='dashed', color='red')
    sns.lineplot(x=test_dates, y=test_predictions, label="Forecast Test", linestyle='dashed', color='purple')
    plt.xlabel("Fecha")
    plt.ylabel("Cumulative Return")
    plt.title("Predicción ARIMA con Rolling Forecasting para Cumulative_Return")
    plt.legend()
    plt.show()

    return {
        "validación": {"MAPE": mape_val, "MAE": mae_val, "MSE": mse_val, "RMSE": rmse_val, "R²": r2_val},
        "test": {"MAPE": mape_test, "MAE": mae_test, "MSE": mse_test, "RMSE": rmse_test, "R²": r2_test},
        "residuals": model_fit.resid  # Se retornan los residuos para la segunda parte
    }

# Definir los tamaños de los conjuntos
train_size = int(len(df) * 0.6)  # 60% entrenamiento
val_size = int(len(df) * 0.2)  # 20% validación
test_size = len(df) - (train_size + val_size)  # 20% test

# Parámetros del modelo ARIMA
best_order = (0, 1, 0)  # Se puede ajustar según análisis previo

# Ejecutar el modelo con rolling forecasting para `Cumulative_Return`
resultados = arima_rolling(df, train_size, val_size, best_order)

# Guardar los residuos para la segunda parte
residuals = resultados["residuals"]

# Pruebas estadísticas sobre residuos
ljung_box_pvalue = acorr_ljungbox(residuals, lags=[10], return_df=True)['lb_pvalue'].values[0]
jarque_bera_pvalue = jarque_bera(residuals)[1]

# Mostrar métricas
print("\nErrores en validación:")
for metric, value in resultados["validación"].items():
    print(f"{metric}: {value:.4f}")

print("\nErrores en test:")
for metric, value in resultados["test"].items():
    print(f"{metric}: {value:.4f}")

print("\nPruebas de hipótesis sobre residuos:")
print(f"Ljung-Box (p-value): {ljung_box_pvalue:.4f}")
print(f"Jarque-Bera (p-value): {jarque_bera_pvalue:.4f}")

# Configurar la figura en formato 2x2
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 10))

# Histograma de residuos
sns.histplot(residuals, bins=30, kde=True, ax=axes[0, 0], color='navy')
axes[0, 0].axvline(x=0, color='red', linestyle='dashed')  # Línea vertical en 0
axes[0, 0].set_title("Histograma de Residuos")
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel("Valor del Residuo")
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel("Frecuencia")

# QQPlot de los residuos
sm.qqplot(residuals, line='s', ax=axes[0, 1])
axes[0, 1].set_title("QQ Plot de Residuos")

# Autocorrelación de residuos (ACF)
plot_acf(residuals, ax=axes[1, 0], lags=20)
axes[1, 0].set_title("Función de Autocorrelación (ACF)")

# Autocorrelación parcial de residuos (PACF)
plot_pacf(residuals, ax=axes[1, 1], lags=20)
axes[1, 1].set_title("Función de Autocorrelación Parcial (PACF)")

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

R²: 0.9983

    test = df['Volatility_14d'][train_size + val_size:].tolist()

    val_dates = df.index[train_size:train_size + val_size]
    test_dates = df.index[train_size + val_size:]

    # Predicciones en validación y test con rolling forecasting
    val_predictions = []
    test_predictions = []

    # Fase de validación (rolling forecasting)
    for t in range(len(val)):
        model = ARIMA(train, order=order)
        model_fit = model.fit()
        forecast = model_fit.forecast()[0]  # Predicción de un solo punto
        val_predictions.append(forecast)
        train.append(val[t])  # Agregar el valor real para continuar el rolling

    # Evaluación en validación
    mae_val = mean_absolute_error(val, val_predictions)
    mse_val = mean_squared_error(val, val_predictions)
    rmse_val = np.sqrt(mse_val)
    mape_val = mean_absolute_percentage_error(val, val_predictions)
    r2_val = r2_score(val, val_predictions)

    # Fase de test (rolling forecasting)
    for t in range(len(test)):
        model = ARIMA(train, order=order)
        model_fit = model.fit()
        forecast = model_fit.forecast()[0]  # Predicción de un solo punto
        test_predictions.append(forecast)
        train.append(test[t])  # Agregar el valor real para continuar el rolling

    # Evaluación en test
    mae_test = mean_absolute_error(test, test_predictions)
    mse_test = mean_squared_error(test, test_predictions)
    rmse_test = np.sqrt(mse_test)
    mape_test = mean_absolute_percentage_error(test, test_predictions)
    r2_test = r2_score(test, test_predictions)

    # Visualización del modelo ARIMA
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
    sns.lineplot(x=df.index[:train_size], y=df['Volatility_14d'][:train_size], label="Train", color='blue')
    sns.lineplot(x=val_dates, y=val, label="Validation", color='orange')
    sns.lineplot(x=test_dates, y=test, label="Test", color='green')
    sns.lineplot(x=val_dates, y=val_predictions, label="Forecast Validation", linestyle='dashed', color='red')
    sns.lineplot(x=test_dates, y=test_predictions, label="Forecast Test", linestyle='dashed', color='purple')
    plt.xlabel("Fecha")
    plt.ylabel("Volatility_14d")
    plt.title("Predicción ARIMA con Rolling Forecasting para Volatility_14d")
    plt.legend()
    plt.show()

    return {
        "validación": {"MAPE": mape_val, "MAE": mae_val, "MSE": mse_val, "RMSE": rmse_val, "R²": r2_val},
        "test": {"MAPE": mape_test, "MAE": mae_test, "MSE": mse_test, "RMSE": rmse_test, "R²": r2_test},
        "residuals": model_fit.resid  # Se retornan los residuos para la segunda parte
    }

# Definir los tamaños de los conjuntos
train_size = int(len(df) * 0.6)  # 60% entrenamiento
val_size = int(len(df) * 0.2)  # 20% validación
test_size = len(df) - (train_size + val_size)  # 20% test

# Parámetros del modelo ARIMA
best_order = (0, 1, 0)  # Se puede ajustar según análisis previo

# Ejecutar el modelo con rolling forecasting para `Volatility_14d`
resultados = arima_rolling(df, train_size, val_size, best_order)

# Guardar los residuos para la segunda parte
residuals = resultados["residuals"]

# Pruebas estadísticas sobre residuos
ljung_box_pvalue = acorr_ljungbox(residuals, lags=[10], return_df=True)['lb_pvalue'].values[0]
jarque_bera_pvalue = jarque_bera(residuals)[1]

# Mostrar métricas

# Histograma de residuos

axes[0, 0].axvline(x=0, color='red', linestyle='dashed')  # Línea vertical en 0
axes[0, 0].set_title("Histograma de Residuos")
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel("Valor del Residuo")
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel("Frecuencia")

# QQPlot de los residuos
sm.qqplot(residuals, line='s', ax=axes[0, 1])
